newsitem.title: USA: Household International to buy Transamerica unit.
newsitem.headline: Household International to buy Transamerica unit.

text.p: Household International Inc said Wednesday it had signed a definitive agreement to purchase Transamerica Corp's consumer finance business for $1.1 billion in cash.
Household said it expects the purchase to be accretive to earnings beginning with the current fiscal year.

With this agreement, Household said it will make significant progress toward achieving its goal of expanding the HFC consumer finance branch network. The company will operate the acquired branches under the HFC brand.
Household said it intends to finance the purchase with a combination of debt and new common equity.

The transaction will not increase Household's financial leverage and will improve its efficiency ratio, it said. The acquisition also will add to its core group of customers and to its growth, it said.
The purchase will build Household's portfolio of core real estate-secured receivables by $3 billion, or almost 38 percent, and will bring Household's total managed assets to over $50 billion.
The purchase excludes delinquent receivables, it added.
Household said the economies of scale provided by the combined operations will result in significant cost savings.
The companies anticipate closing prior to June 30.

"This acquisition brings us a very high-quality portfolio of real estate-secured loans, a great branch network, and many talented employees," William Aldinger, chairman of Household, said in a statement. "It allows us to achieve additional top-line growth by focusing on our core customer while improving our efficiency ratio."
Frank Herringer, chairman of Transamerica, said the deal was good for his company's shareholders.

Household, through its subsidiaries, provides consumer financial services. One of its primary businesses is HFC, the oldest U.S. consumer finance company. Household is also one of the largest issuers of private-label and general purpose credit cards in the U.S. Its principal cards include the GM Card and the AFL-CIO's Union Privilege card.
San Francisco-based Transamerica, which had consolidated assets of $50 billion as of March 31, provides specialized financial and life insurance products and services worldwide.
